# Finding the Antiderivative of x³sin(x)

I'll use **integration by parts** repeatedly (the tabular method).

## Setting Up the Tabular Method

I differentiate x³ until it reaches 0, and integrate sin(x) the same number of times:

| Sign | Derivatives of x³ | Integrals of sin(x) |
|:----:|:-----------------:|:-------------------:|
| +    | x³               | -cos(x)            |
| −    | 3x²              | -sin(x)            |
| +    | 6x               | cos(x)             |
| −    | 6                | sin(x)             |

## Applying the Formula

$$\int x^3 \sin(x)\,dx = (+)(x^3)(-\cos x) + (-)(3x^2)(-\sin x) + (+)(6x)(\cos x) + (-)(6)(\sin x) + C$$

$$= -x^3\cos(x) + 3x^2\sin(x) + 6x\cos(x) - 6\sin(x) + C$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result:
- d/dx[-x³cos(x)] = -3x²cos(x) + x³sin(x)
- d/dx[3x²sin(x)] = 6xsin(x) + 3x²cos(x)
- d/dx[6xcos(x)] = 6cos(x) - 6xsin(x)
- d/dx[-6sin(x)] = -6cos(x)

**Sum:** x³sin(x) + (-3x²cos(x) + 3x²cos(x)) + (6xsin(x) - 6xsin(x)) + (6cos(x) - 6cos(x)) = x³sin(x) ✓

<answer>-x**3*cos(x) + 3*x**2*sin(x) + 6*x*cos(x) - 6*sin(x) + C</answer>
